payload.answer: [hard] Do NOT invent a second locking scheme alongside the existing advisory locks and leases. Two coordination mechanisms over the same resources is worse than either alone -- extend what exists or explain why it cannot be extended. [hard] Never block a worker on a human: any coordination must be lock-with-timeout or lease-based, never a wait for input. [hard] Every job stays idempotent under replay; a worker can die mid-parallel-run and another must resume safely. [hard] No deadlocks: if the design introduces any ordering between locks, state the total order that makes deadlock impossible. [hard] PostgreSQL is the only coordination substrate -- no Redis, no files-as-locks, no in-process-only state that dies with the worker. [hard] 100% branch coverage including the contention paths; concurrency code with untested contention is untested code. [soft] The 'chat mechanism' idea from the request is worth evaluating and probably rejecting: agents negotiating for resources is far more failure-prone than a lock, and it cannot be tested deterministically.
